case.description: Design a removable joint for a 300 mm inspection hatch on a dry tabletop trough fixture. A technician must open it repeatedly while retaining the existing hatch, rim and seal. All dimensions and observations below are stipulated for this hypothetical fixture.
case.valued_outcome: After ten opening cycles, the closed hatch stays within 1 mm of its marked position, withstands a supplied 20 N sideways pull, and can be reopened by one technician within 30 seconds.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, glue or permanently deform the hatch or trough.
Keep the full marked inspection opening unobstructed when open.
Use no powered mechanism; loose components must remain recoverable.
The seal must show no new visible tears after testing.
resources: One 300 by 180 mm hatch, one trough rim and one 2 mm removable seal.
Four 100 by 25 by 3 mm aluminum strips, two 250 mm fabric straps, six M4 bolts with nuts, four rubber pads and 1 m of cord.
One hand drill usable only on supplied strips, one hacksaw, two spanners, ruler and marker.
Ninety minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for observation.
observations: The untreated hatch slides 4 mm under the 20 N pull.
The seal leaves a continuous contact mark when the hatch is centered.
Awkward observation: pressing the hatch more tightly at its left corner makes the opposite corner lift 2 mm; this occurred in three supplied trials.

openings.claim: Eccentric left pressure elastically twists the hatch. Centered seal contact can coexist with twisting; untreated lateral sliding reflects inadequate restraint.
openings.delta: Change the pressure carrier to a removable strip stiffener lashed solely to the hatch; reversible padded rim clamps supply lateral restraint.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, seal/rim fulcrum rocking, adding stiffness at unchanged bearings and equal left force reduces opposite-corner lift.
openings.probe: Use the shared matched comparison below; defeat this explanation if adequate stiffening leaves lift unchanged.
assumptions: Strip stiffness and secure cord lashing are sufficient; hatch-only attachment adds no rim bearing.
Rim geometry permits removable clamps without damage; neither is supplied.

openings.claim: A raised seal/rim bearing makes the hatch rock diagonally. The compliant seal can mark continuously when centered while permitting rocking and sideways slip.
openings.delta: Change the closure dependency from increasing strap tension to clearance-limited padded strip clamps, keeping the seal and permitting removable bearing adjustment.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, elastic hatch twisting, hatch-only stiffening preserves approximately 2 mm opposite lift under equal left force because the support fulcrum remains.
openings.probe: Use the same comparison; defeat this explanation if stiffening suppresses lift with bearings demonstrably unchanged. Bearing adjustment remains a subsequent proposal, not deployment.
assumptions: An uneven support exists; continuous contact does not establish it.
Available strips can create clearance stops and sufficient lateral restraint within fabrication time.

artifact.assessment: Probe two reversible configurations differing only by hatch-only stiffening. Apply matched 20 N left pressure with the scale, recording opposite lift by ruler; bearing invariance and useful stiffness must first be established or discrimination fails. Allocate six closure/pull trials per configuration: five normal checks during ten opening cycles, then one right-card disturbed closure. Measure position, 20 N sideways retention, reopening time and visible seal tears against every supplied target. Bound observation to twenty minutes and fabrication to ninety; capacity is unproven. Remove and cord-bundle all joint pieces when open, leaving the marked opening clear. No powered or permanent changes.

openings.claim: Separate lateral registration from downward retention: removable edge stops may resist sliding without the corner pressure that lifts the opposite corner.
openings.delta: Change the load carrier from seal friction under added corner pressure to two externally clamped strip stops registering perpendicular hatch edges. Use four strips as two jaw pairs, supplied bolts and rubber pads; drill only strips. Supplied straps provide modest retention only if their reach and attachment path suffice. Cord tethers removed parts. Remove the hatch and any projecting jaws to clear the entire opening.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: tighter strap retention alone prevents sliding through friction. Edge registration predicts reduced sideways displacement at unchanged modest retention; the rival predicts improvement primarily with increased tension. Persistence of opposite-corner lift or loss of registration with the right-contact card would defeat the proposed separation.
openings.probe: First check rim jaw access, strap reach, stop contact height and clearance without stressing the seal. If constructible within ninety minutes, use one configuration: ten ordinary closure/pull cycles and two final card-disturbed closure/pull trials, twelve total. Record marked displacement, opposite-corner lift, visible seal damage and single-technician reopening time on every trial. Compare displacement against the supplied untreated 4 mm observation; this tests outcome feasibility but cannot isolate causation without a matched rival configuration. Stop on visible damage. Complete observations within twenty minutes; inability to measure the stated differences within that budget defeats probe feasibility.
assumptions: The rim offers accessible surfaces for reversible external jaws; geometry is unprovided.
The supplied strips and bolts can form rigid stops without permanent hatch/rim deformation or excessive pad compression.
The straps reach a usable retaining path; no longer strap or new anchor is assumed.
Stops engage despite card-induced height change; no performance is established.

artifact.assessment: One uncertain opening. Successful trials must satisfy the 1 mm, 20 N, thirty-second and seal-integrity requirements, including the disturbed closures except seal-contact continuity. External-clamp access and strap reach are indispensable unknowns; failure of either parks fabrication rather than relaxing constraints. This is a reversible feasibility probe, not deployment.

openings.claim: A removable joint that transfers sideways load through edge bearing may resist sliding without the corner pressure that lifts the opposite corner.
openings.delta: Replace reliance on seal friction with two opposed paired-strip clamps: lower strips under an accessible rim lip, padded upper strips over the hatch, and external bolts closing the jaws. Arrange clamp edges as lateral abutments against both hatch and rim. Tether removable assemblies with cord and lift them completely clear for inspection. This depends on compatible edge geometry, not supplied proof of it.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, padded clamps relying solely on friction, abutment engagement should stop sideways travel before 1 mm with modest preload. If both arrangements require increased corner pressure and produce the same opposite-corner lift, the proposed separation of shear restraint from closure pressure fails.
openings.probe: First use the ruler and loose strips to check lip access, bolt clearance, protective-pad coverage, abutment contact and full removal; fabricate only if these fit. Use four strips, four pads and at most six bolts, drilling only strips. Mark the centered hatch. Run ten opening/closure/pull cycles, the tenth with the right-contact card. Apply the supplied 20 N pull, measure displacement and opposite-corner lift, time each reopening, and inspect the seal. Stop for damage or insecure engagement. This uses one configuration and ten of twelve permitted trials; existing untreated-slide evidence supplies a limited rival reference.
assumptions: Rim underside and hatch edges permit removable jaws and direct bearing without machining either part.
Strip stiffness, bolt lengths and pad placement allow secure engagement within fabrication time.
The card disturbance does not disengage the abutments or induce unacceptable rocking; test this rather than assume compliance.

artifact.assessment: A candidate probe, not a demonstrated joint. Incompatible geometry, insufficient hardware capacity, new seal tears, displacement above 1 mm, inability to sustain 20 N, or reopening above 30 seconds defeats it. Without compatible geometry, no feasible fabrication is established; the trial cap alone provides no assurance.
